fichas.title: General care ward planning
fichas.summary: Care departments should be enclosed units that avoid through traffic. Patient rooms should receive natural light; central functional and support rooms may be placed in an internal artificially lit area. Ward units should support combination and interdisciplinary operation, with visible, accessible relationships between the entrance, nurses’ station, stores, washrooms, and supply and waste rooms. Provide a doctor’s room and accessible wet cells.
uses: General inpatient care, particularly short-term and acute illnesses
Medication, laundry, waste, and catering logistics

fichas.title: Accessible wet-cell fixture heights
fichas.summary: Each patient room should have its own wet cell with a WC and washbasin, and sometimes a shower; showers may instead be separate. Wet cells should be accessible to disabled people. The text specifies a minimum vanity-unit height/clearance so a wheelchair can fit underneath and an approximate WC height measured to the top of the toilet seat.
